description: This figure group is a single panel: a chemical-composition table rendered as an image (no figure number or row label column is visible in the pixels). The header row lists eight element symbols in bold, each with its own horizontal rule beneath: Si, C, Mn, P, S, Mo, Al, Cu; the caption states the values are in weight percent. Six data rows follow, each giving one steel chemistry. Row 1: Si 1.01, C 0.89, Mn 30.20, P 0.006, S 0.001, Mo 0.31, Al 8.85, Cu –. Row 2: 0.92, 0.94, 29.10, 0.043, 0.006, 0.33, 8.28, 0.09. Row 3: 1.07, 0.90, 29.11, 0.070, –, 0.37, 9.25, 0.10. Row 4: 0.59, 0.95, 30.35, 0.002, 0.006, 0.54, 8.74, 0.01. Row 5: 1.07, 0.90, 30.42, 0.001, 0.006, 0.53, 8.83, 0.006. Row 6: 1.56, 0.89, 29.97, 0.002, 0.007, 0.53, 8.81, 0.006. No alloy identifiers, balance-iron column, or processing/condition labels are printed. The table demonstrates that all six heats form one narrow family of high-manganese, high-aluminium, ~0.9 wt.% C steels, with deliberate minor additions/impurity variation (P, S, Cu, Mo) that define a composition series for comparison.

observations.observation: The table header consists of exactly eight element symbols: Si, C, Mn, P, S, Mo, Al, Cu, each set in bold with its own horizontal rule.
The caption identifies the table as 'Table I. Steel chemistries in weight percent', so all tabulated values are in wt.%.
The table contains six data rows, i.e. six distinct steel chemistries, with no identifier column or row-number labels printed.
Mn is the dominant alloying element in every row, printed as 30.20, 29.10, 29.11, 30.35, 30.42 and 29.97 wt.%.
Al is the second major addition, printed as 8.85, 8.28, 9.25, 8.74, 8.83 and 8.81 wt.% across the six rows.
C is nearly constant at 0.89, 0.94, 0.90, 0.95, 0.90 and 0.89 wt.% across the six rows.
Si varies most among the major elements: 1.01, 0.92, 1.07, 0.59, 1.07 and 1.56 wt.%.
Mo is a minor addition in all rows, printed as 0.31, 0.33, 0.37, 0.54, 0.53 and 0.53 wt.%.
Cu is listed as '- -' (not measured/absent) only in row 1; the other rows give 0.09, 0.10, 0.01, 0.006 and 0.006 wt.%.
S is listed as '-' in row 3 and printed as 0.001, 0.006, 0.006 and 0.007 wt.% in rows 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6.
P is lowest in rows 4-6 (0.002, 0.001, 0.002 wt.%) and highest in row 3 (0.070 wt.%).
No iron/balance column and no processing or heat-treatment condition is printed anywhere in the table.
The citing abstract describes fully austenitic cast steels with nominal composition Fe-30%Mn-9%Al-0.9%C and 4-12 wt.% Al, which matches the central tendency of the tabulated Mn, Al and C values.

unreadable_items: No sample/alloy identifier column is present in the tabulated pixels, so the six chemistries cannot be mapped to the sample names used elsewhere in the paper
Row 1 Cu and row 3 S are rendered as a dash ('-'), which the image alone cannot distinguish between 'not measured' and 'below detection limit'
